newsitem.title: GERMANY: Organisers raise glass to successful Oktoberfest.
newsitem.headline: Organisers raise glass to successful Oktoberfest.

text.p: This year's Oktoberfest attracted around 6.9 million visitors, 200,000 more than last year, organisers said on Sunday as Munich's annual celebration of beer and bratwurst drew to a close.
Revellers got through 300,000 more litres of beer than their counterparts last year, downing 5.1 million litres during the 16-day festival.
"This was a successful Oktoberfest without any major problems," mayor Christian Ude told a news conference, hailing the attendance figures as the highest for more than 10 years.
Although the total number of visitors was just under the seven million target, peak days were so packed that organisers had to appeal to people to stay away from the festival site.
The congestion prompted calls for the Oktoberfest to be moved from "the meadows", its city-centre parkland home, to a larger out-of-town site or for the duration to be extended.
But Ude rejected those suggestions. "The Oktoberfest is a fixture in the Munich calendar, and at this location," he said.
He said much of the overcrowding could be avoided if soccer matches were not scheduled in Munich on Saturdays during the Oktoberfest.

The matches draw thousands of visiting fans to the city, who promptly make a beeline for the meadows as soon as the final whistle goes in the Olympic Stadium to either drown their sorrows or toast their success.
The only accident of note at this year's festival occurred last week, when two carriages in a rollercoaster ride collided, causing mainly slight injuries to 25 people.
Organisers have been keen to build up a picture of typical Okoberfest visitors and their research shows they are most likely to be young, male and -- if not German -- Italian.
